truths.truth: For the same trigger, `route.mjs resolve` returns a different cross-model tier AND effort at solo vs shipped vs critical, both beside `reviewers`
truths.evidence: Live: `node cadence-core/bin/route.mjs resolve --role cad-reviewer --file <cfg>` with stakes solo/shipped/critical returned reviewer_tiers.plan cheap/balanced/flagship and reviewer_efforts.plan low/medium/high; risk_surface identical ladder; both maps keyed exactly like `reviewers`. Source rows at cadence-core/route-table.json:59-69 (tiers) and :71-75 (efforts); emitted at cadence-core/bin/route.mjs:724.

truths.truth: The value is traced end to end: route-table.json grid -> route.mjs resolve envelope -> the prose that consumes it (review-provider `--model`/`--effort`)
truths.evidence: cadence-core/references/review-triggers.md:233-241 takes `reviewer_tiers[<trigger>]`/`reviewer_efforts[<trigger>]` off the step-1 resolve line, indexes `review.providers.<name>.tiers` with the tier, and passes both to `review-provider.mjs review --model <model> --effort <effort>`; reach rows cadence-core/references/config-reach.md:163-174 name the same handoff.

truths.truth: `self-verify` reports no `missing-cell` for either the `tiers` or the `efforts` grid, walked in both directions
truths.evidence: `node cadence-core/bin/self-verify.mjs` exit 0, `problems: []`, `routing-cells` among checks run. The walk is real, not vacuous: cadence-core/bin/lib/route-cells.mjs:302-350 runs the same two-direction walk over both grids per level (absent block, absent row, absent (level,trigger) cell -> `missing-cell`; unknown trigger -> `unknown-trigger`; out-of-vocabulary value -> `unknown-tier`/`unknown-effort`).

truths.truth: On a repo where no layer sets it, `config.mjs get review.triggers.plan.tier` reports the value the resolver actually uses at the effective stakes level
truths.evidence: `node cadence-core/bin/config.mjs get review.triggers.plan.tier` answers `{"values":{"review.triggers.plan.tier":null},"warnings":["... is unset: no config layer pins this model tier, so the stakes level decides it - `route.mjs resolve` answers it for a level"]}`. It no longer answers a fixed `flagship` (schema default is now the null sentinel), but it does not report the resolved value either. cadence-core/bin/config.mjs:288-291 states this is deliberate: "It never states what the level fires and never reads route-table.json (D-07): this seam does not know the stakes level".

truths.truth: `git.create_tag` is read at exactly one prose site (the land-time tag cut), its schema purpose no longer names the milestone close, and a close with `create_tag:false` still bumps the plugin manifest
truths.evidence: `grep -rn create_tag cadence-core/ skills/`: the only prose readers are skills/cad-land/SKILL.md:26,183,193 (one site, the tag cut); cadence-core/workflows/milestone.md contains no occurrence, and its step 2 (lines 24-40) decides release mode from `git-branch.mjs tags` + a confirmed version, with "No config key decides this". Schema purpose cadence-core/config.schema.json:51 = "Cut the release tag at land ... It governs that tag cut and nothing else: no other step reads it, and a manifest bump never depends on it". Behaviour: fixture with `.planning/config.json` `{"git":{"create_tag":false}}` (confirmed read back as false) then `release-bump.mjs bump --dir <fix> --version 1.1.0` -> `action:"bumped"`, manifest version 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0.

Arm at cadence-core/bin/git-branch.mjs:94-95 (`readTags(dir, dir)`), dispatched at :110-111.

gaps.name: Unset tier reports the resolved value; grids have no missing cells
gaps.reason: behavior wrong (half the item): the grids half holds - self-verify walks both `tiers` and `efforts` in both directions per level and reports no `missing-cell`. The read half does not: with no layer setting it, `config.mjs get review.triggers.plan.tier` answers `null` plus a warning pointing at `route.mjs resolve`, not the value the resolver uses at the effective stakes level. It no longer answers a fixed `flagship`, so the lie is gone, but the item as written asks for the resolved value and that value is unobtainable from this seam by design.
gaps.evidence: `node cadence-core/bin/config.mjs get review.triggers.plan.tier` -> {"values":{"review.triggers.plan.tier":null},"warnings":["review.triggers.plan.tier is unset: no config layer pins this model tier, so the stakes level decides it - `route.mjs resolve` answers it for a level"]} (same shape for `.effort` and, unchanged, `.gate`). cadence-core/bin/config.mjs:236-296 implements it and :288-291 states the refusal outright: "It never states what the level fires and never reads route-table.json (D-07): this seam does not know the stakes level, and answering as if it did is the same defect pointed the other way." CONTEXT.md D-04 licenses the null sentinel; AC2's wording and D-04/D-07 are in tension and SUMMARY.md records no deviation for it.
gaps.missing: One decision, then one edit. Either (a) reword AC2 / UAT item 2 to what was deliberately built - an unset read answers the null sentinel and names `route.mjs resolve` as the answering seam, rather than a fixed `flagship` - and record it as a deviation in SUMMARY.md; or (b) if the literal criterion is meant to stand, give the read the level: have `config.mjs get` resolve a level-keyed unset key through route-table.json (which D-07 currently forbids) so the answer carries the tier the resolver would use.
